extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners (primary); patent applicants and practitioners (secondary)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for when and how an examiner may make an Office action final (including first/second-action rules), what must be stated in a final rejection, handling of replies, withdrawal of finality, time limits (shortened statutory period), advisory actions, examiner's amendments, and required form paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to make a final rejection (37 CFR 1.113)
rubrics_metrics.description: On the second or any subsequent examination or consideration by the examiner the rejection or other action may be made final, whereupon applicant's reply is limited to appeal or to amendment as specified. Petition may be taken to the Commissioner for objections or requirements not involved in the rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replies to a final rejection must comply with § 1.114 or paragraph (c) of 37 CFR 1.113. For final actions in inter partes reexamination see § 1.953. Form paragraph 7.39 is used to conclude the final rejection letter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner must state and repeat all grounds and reasons
rubrics_metrics.description: In making such final rejection, the examiner shall repeat or state all grounds of rejection then considered applicable to the claims in the application, clearly stating the reasons in support thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All outstanding grounds of rejection of record should be carefully reviewed and any such grounds relied on in the final rejection should be reiterated and clearly developed so applicant may judge advisability of an appeal. If a single previous Office action contains a complete statement, the final rejection may refer to it but should include a rebuttal to applicant's arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply to a final rejection must cancel or appeal each rejected claim
rubrics_metrics.description: Reply to a final rejection or action must include cancellation of, or appeal from the rejection of, each rejected claim. If any claim stands allowed, the reply must comply with any requirements or objections as to form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing an amendment after final does not stop the running of the statutory period for reply unless the examiner holds the claims to be in condition for allowance. Failure to file a proper Notice of Appeal within the reply period (or obtain an extension) results in abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop a clear issue before making final rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Before final rejection is in order a clear issue should be developed between the examiner and applicant; the invention should be thoroughly searched in the first action and the references fully applied; applicant should amend to avoid all grounds of rejection and objection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Switching subject matter in successive amendments or switching reference sets in successive rejections tends to defeat the goal of reaching a clearly defined issue for early termination (allowance or final rejection). Examiners should avoid hasty and ill-considered final rejections; applicants are entitled to a full and fair hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second-or-later-action finality exception for new grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Second or any subsequent actions on the merits shall be final, except where the examiner introduces a new ground of rejection that is neither necessitated by applicant's amendment of the claims nor based on information submitted in an IDS filed during the 37 CFR 1.97(c) period with fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where an IDS with fee is filed in the permitted period, the examiner may use the submitted information and make the next Office action final (provided no other new ground not necessitated by amendment is introduced). In reexamination, a second/subsequent action should not be made final if it includes a rejection on newly cited art other than IDS-submitted information of any claim not amended by applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not make final when rejection relies on prior art not of record for amended claims
rubrics_metrics.description: A second or any subsequent action on the merits should not be made final if it includes a rejection, on prior art not of record, of any claim amended to include limitations which should reasonably have been expected to be claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112 for incompleteness that would reasonably be replied to by an amendment supplying the omitted element should not be made final.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special considerations for 35 U.S.C. 102(e)/103 references (common ownership)
rubrics_metrics.description: When applying any 35 U.S.C. 102(e)/103 references against claims of an application filed on or after Nov 29, 1999, the examiner should anticipate that a statement averring common ownership at the time the invention was made may disqualify any patent or application applied in a rejection under 103 based on 102(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If such ownership statement is filed in reply and claims are not amended, the examiner may not make the next Office action final if a new rejection is made. See MPEP § 706.02(l)(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: First-action final rejection in continuing/substitute applications
rubrics_metrics.description: A first Office action in a continuing or substitute application may be finally rejected where (A) the new application is a continuing application of, or a substitute for, an earlier application, and (B) all claims are drawn to the same invention claimed in the earlier application and would have been properly finally rejected on the grounds and art of record in the next Office action if they had been entered in the earlier application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A first-action final may not be made final where the new application contains material that was presented in the earlier application after final rejection or closing of prosecution but was denied entry because (A) new issues required further consideration/search, or (B) new matter issues were raised. In a CIP, a first-action final is improper where any claim includes subject matter not present in the earlier application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use appropriate form paragraphs for final actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph 7.40 should be used where an action is made final including new grounds of rejection necessitated by applicant's amendment; other specialized form paragraphs (7.39, 7.39.01, 7.41, 7.41.03, 7.42.09, etc.) are prescribed for various finality contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 7.39 (Action Is Final) and 7.39.01 (Final Rejection, Options for Applicant, Pro Se) include statutory period and extension information and must be used/preceded as directed. Use PTOL-326 Office Action Summary in all Office actions up to and including final rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prematureness of final rejection must be raised while application pending
rubrics_metrics.description: Any question as to prematureness of a final rejection should be raised, if at all, while the application is still pending before the primary examiner; it is a question of practice distinct from tenability of the rejection and may not be advanced as a ground for appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prematureness is reviewable by petition under 37 CFR 1.181 (see MPEP § 1002.02(c)). If the examiner finds the final rejection premature on reconsideration, the finality should be withdrawn while the application is still pending (use Form Paragraph 7.42). The examiner cannot vacate finality once the application is abandoned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of final rejection — when permissible and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a final rejection that is not premature has been entered, it should not be withdrawn at applicant's request except on a showing under 37 CFR 1.116(b). Further amendment or argument will be considered in certain instances; amendments placing the application in condition for allowance or complying with form objections are permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner may withdraw rejection if new facts or reasons convince examiner that claims are allowable. Withdrawal to apply a new ground is permissible but should be limited to situations where a new reference fully meets at least one claim or meets it except for differences shown to be completely obvious. Practice should not be used for subsidiary/ cumulative references. When a final rejection is withdrawn, amendments filed after final are ordinarily entered. New grounds after an appeal brief require supervisory approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: New grounds in reopened prosecution require supervisory approval
rubrics_metrics.description: New grounds of rejection made in an Office action reopening prosecution after the filing of an appeal brief require the approval of the supervisory patent examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shortened statutory period (SSP) and variable reply period rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Final rejections typically set a 3-month shortened statutory period (SSP) for reply; if applicant files a first reply within 2 months of mailing of the final action and the advisory action is not mailed until after the end of the 3-month period, the SSP will expire on the mailing date of the advisory action. In no event shall the statutory period for reply expire later than six months from the mailing date of the final action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the form paragraph setting a variable reply period is omitted, the SSP ends 3 months from the date of final action and can only be extended by petition under 37 CFR 1.136(a). The variable-reply procedure does not apply where SSP less than 3 months is set (e.g., reissue litigation applications or reexamination). If the 2-month cutoff falls on a weekend/holiday and reply is filed next business day, reply is deemed within 2 months for variable-period purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory action duties when first reply filed within 2 months
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant files a complete first reply within 2 months, the examiner must determine if the reply (1) places the application in condition for allowance, (2) places in condition for allowance except for matters of form, or (3) does not place the application in condition for allowance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If (1) or (2), process as allowance and no extension fees are due. If (3), the advisory action should inform applicant that the SSP expires 3 months from the final rejection or on the mailing date of the advisory action, whichever is later, by using PTOL-303 or Form Paragraph 7.67.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of form paragraphs 7.67.01 and 7.67.02 for advisory actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph 7.67.01 is used when first reply is filed within two months and the advisory action must notify applicant of the SSP expiration; Form paragraph 7.67.02 is used to vacate/reset a three-month SSP when no variable SSP was set in the final but a first reply was filed within two months and the advisory action was not mailed within three months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When correctly used, the time for taking further action begins to run 3 months from the final rejection or from the advisory action, whichever is later; extension fees are calculated from the date the SSP expires as set forth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner's amendments after first reply and extension fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a complete first reply to a final Office action has been filed within 2 months, an examiner's amendment to place the application in condition for allowance may be made without payment of extension fees even if the amendment is made more than 3 months from the final action. An examiner's amendment may not be made more than 6 months from the final action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a complete first reply was not filed within 2 months, applicant's authorization to make an amendment placing the application in condition for allowance must be within the 3-month SSP or within an extended period obtained by petition and fee under 37 CFR 1.136(a). Formal matters identified for the first time after a reply and requiring applicant correction may be required in an Ex parte Quayle action and normally do not require extension fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of time under 37 CFR 1.136(a) — petition and authorization rules
rubrics_metrics.description: An extension of time under 37 CFR 1.136(a) requires a petition for an extension and the appropriate fee provided in 37 CFR 1.17. Applicant may authorize the examiner to make the petition of record and charge a deposit account; such authorization must be made of record before the extended period expires and must be recorded in an examiner's amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office employees may not accept oral instructions to charge credit cards for patent process fees. The examiner's amendment should indicate person making authorization, when given, deposit account number, length of extension requested and amount to be charged. Use Form Paragraph 13.02.02 when authorized by telephone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice for replies after final — processing and consideration limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Replies after final should be processed and considered promptly. They should not be considered by the examiner unless filed within the SSP or accompanied by a petition for extension and appropriate fee. This applies to supplemental replies filed after the first reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interviews may be conducted after expiration of the SSP but within the 6-month statutory period without payment of an extension fee. If prosecution is to be reopened after a final Office action has been replied to, the finality should be withdrawn to avoid abandonment and payment of extension fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on withdrawing finality to apply new grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Withdrawal of finality to apply a new ground of rejection is permissible only in limited circumstances — normally where a new reference either fully meets at least one claim or meets it except for differences shown to be completely obvious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The practice should not be used for application of subsidiary, cumulative, or merely 'better' references. When withdrawing finality for a new ground, withdrawal should normally be limited to the claims involved and amendments filed after final are ordinarily entered when finality is withdrawn.
